title: Hagwon Street
description:
10 PM — the hagwon district in Daechi-dong.
Middle and high school students pour out of cram schools.

Math, English, science, essay writing...
Parents in this neighborhood reportedly spend a third of their Gangnam mortgage payments on education.

choices.text: Even as an adult, you think: I should be learning something
choices.result_text:
No money for hagwon. Decided to start with YouTube.

Seoul has the highest density of learning opportunities in Korea.
Knowing how to find the right content is a skill in itself.

choices.text: Wonder what kind of adults these kids will become
choices.result_text:
How many of those kids will end up living the life they actually want?

You're chasing Gangnam too — you're also a product of that same competition.
Korean education and Korean real estate share the same root.

title: College Entrance Exam Day
description:
Third Thursday of November.
Fighter jets pause their flights. The stock market opened an hour late.

The entire nation pressed pause
for one exam taken by eighteen-year-olds.

choices.text: Send a good-luck message to anyone you know taking it
choices.result_text:
Sent 'do well' to your younger cousin.

You remembered your own exam day. You can still conjure the smell of that morning.
Every Korean has a memory of this day.

choices.text: Don't think about the noise — get your own work done
choices.result_text:
Suneung is Suneung, your work is your work.

But somewhere out there, someone is filling in answer bubbles right now.
Thought about that, and wanted to be a little more diligent yourself.

title: The Exam Preppers
description:
Same goshiwon — the person next door is studying for a government exam.
Their light never goes off, even at 3 AM.

Administrative exam, bar exam, public service exam.
Some people hold on here for years.

choices.text: Say something — a sense of solidarity in shared circumstances
choices.result_text:
'Hope it goes well for you.' Brief exchange in the hallway.
'Thanks. You too.' Came back.

We don't know each other's names. Still — the warmest exchange in this goshiwon hallway.

Passed the lit room without stopping.

How many years has that light been on?
Have I ever thrown myself into something that completely?

title: First Day at English Class
description:
Enrolled in an English academy to build credentials.
Most students are office workers. Class starts at 7:30 PM.

The teacher asks everyone to introduce themselves.
'My name is... I am... working at...'

choices.text: Commit to going for three months
choices.result_text:
Signed up for three months. ₩300,000.

Embarrassing at first. After a month, words started coming.
Language starts improving the moment you stop being embarrassed.

choices.text: Do it yourself with an app — the tuition isn't worth it
choices.result_text:
Installed Duolingo. Free.

Ten minutes a day became a habit. Slow, but consistent.
Some things can be done for free.
